{"self_assessment": "Impact
I built the bottom tail (stroke 4), a visible part of the fish's silhouette. I started it as soon as the belly reached the lower notch and laid it in about five minutes of continuous work, and it fell dark. The fish body, nose and lower tail read clearly, and by my read of the table about 105 of the 120 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution
I worked quietly and steadily on a single stroke, tracing it from the pad so the curve matched the plan. I then inspected the tail edge several times. On one of those checks I found that the last dark domino on the belly side pointed up but the next one sat off its path, and I passed that to Omar with a specific suggestion of what to nudge.

Collaboration
I kept the table updated on what I saw. I offered to take the top of the tail so Omar could hold the bridge. I kept my hands away from the busy spots so we didn't bump each other's work, and I credited the team's work in the final check.

Leadership
I took ownership of my stroke without needing direction and finished it on time. When the team agreed to stop touching the tail near the end, I backed that and kept my hands off, which kept the standing picture stable for the push. I also kept morale up with a clear, positive call that we had a proper fish.", "my_share_percent": 25}
